summary: cron options: backup, cron_file in /etc/cron.d (must be module-managed, requires user), day, disabled, env, hour and insertafter for environment variables.
questions: How do I put a cron job in /etc/cron.d instead of a user crontab?
How do I comment out (disable) a cron job without deleting it?
How do I back up the crontab before changing it?
What filename characters are allowed in /etc/cron.d?

answer_card.title: cron parameters (part 1)
answer_card.answer_md:
- `cron_file`: use a file (relative paths → `/etc/cron.d`) instead of a user crontab. Requires `user` (unless absent). Must be exclusively managed by the module; **never** use for `/etc/crontab`. Filenames: letters, digits, `_`, `-` only.
- `disabled` (false): comment out the job (with `state=present`)
- `backup` (false)
- `day` (dom), `hour`: default `*`
- `env`: manage an env var instead of a job; `insertafter` to position it
